entities.rationale: Stable, peaceful middle-income island with good institutions; main local risks are cyclones, imported food and fuel, and debt, so collapse is mostly the global floor and near-free essentials need cheap global supply from superintelligence.

Extreme heat, scarce water, near-total food imports and a volatile Horn of Africa neighbourhood with weak governance make a long loss of water, food or security plausible; foreign bases and port income are the main buffers.
Currently stable but with a coup history, cyclones, sea-level rise and weak water and health outcomes (life expectancy 67.5); abundance would require large outside cost declines.
Very poor, coup-prone, with very weak government effectiveness, high fertility, food insecurity and cyclone exposure; a prolonged food or health breakdown is the most likely path to collapse.
Poor, with 27% undernourishment, weak state capacity, a record of ethnic unrest and riots, great-power rivalry and high climate vulnerability; food and security are the weak points.

Oil wealth can pay for sea walls and services, but a population on a coastal plain below sea level, high crime, ethnic politics, resource-curse risk and the Venezuelan border claim keep collapse well above the floor.

Very stable with abundant hydropower, but exposed to glacial-lake floods and to China-India tension; middle income and heavy emigration limit the chance of near-free essentials without superintelligence.

Extremely rich, well governed and embedded in the EU, so collapse is mostly global doom; its very high income makes it one of the few places where essentials could fall below 10% of income, though its income per resident is inflated by cross-border workers and health costs rise with aging.

Rich and orderly but completely dependent on mainland China for water, food and power, with a volatile casino economy, the world's lowest fertility, typhoons and low-lying reclaimed land; a Taiwan conflict is the main local tail risk.
Coming offshore oil could ease a heavy debt load, but a low-lying coastal capital, middling governance and a coup history leave moderate collapse risk and little chance of near-free essentials.
A NATO member close to EU accession with decent incomes, so collapse risk is low apart from Balkan tensions and rapid aging; abundance depends on EU-level cost declines.
A rich, safe EU island whose weak points are imported energy, desalinated water and imported food; with cheap superintelligence-driven energy those weak points mostly disappear.

Islands about a metre above sea level facing 0.5 m or more of rise, salinized freshwater, heavy debt and reliance on tourism; built-up islands such as Hulhumale and better engineering are the main defences.
One of Africa's most stable democracies, but drought-prone, dependent on desalination and food imports, and heavily indebted; water and food are the pillars at risk.

A wealthy, low-debt, stable energy exporter with plenty of water; the risks are oil depletion, a royal succession, imported food and South China Sea tension, and a life expectancy of 75.5 leaves little margin on health.
Gang violence is high (28 homicides per 100,000), Guatemala claims its territory, and hurricanes and a low-lying coast add risk; security is the most fragile pillar.
A high-income tourism economy on very low islands in the hurricane belt (Dorian was a warning), with high crime and interest costs taking 20% of revenue; it is close to the US for recovery support.

The world's most peaceful country, with cheap geothermal and hydro power, abundant water and strong institutions, so collapse is mostly global doom; the tail risks are volcanoes, imported food and a possible slowdown of the Atlantic overturning circulation.
Among the most disaster-exposed countries on Earth (cyclones, volcanoes, earthquakes), poor, with low electricity and water access and weak government effectiveness, although it is peaceful.
A stable, well-run democracy with high readiness to adapt, but it is water-scarce, imports food and fuel, carries heavy debt and is exposed to hurricanes; water is the weakest pillar.
